definitions.meaning: to be called in and told off by a superior
describes a room whose floor has been laid with a fitted rug

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for laying something over the floorboards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being called onto the boss's rug for a scolding gives one sense; a floor laid with rug material gives the other.

definitions.meaning: to sing joyfully, as at Christmas
a joyful religious song, especially a Christmas one

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for festive singing and the noun for a seasonal song of praise.

definitions.meaning: a building where plays are staged
a toy house or den children play in

explanation.surface: A theatre puts on something juvenile.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for staging plays, and a small toy home children amuse themselves in.

clue.text: Puzzle how to beat a lightweight

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gram is a tiny unit of weight

explanation.surface: A question of how a heavier fighter can defeat a featherweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how to' is link wording; 'beat' and 'lightweight' suggest boxing, but they give a thrashing and a small metric weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese dissection puzzle in which seven flat shapes are arranged into figures.

parts.note: definite means exact or precise
an article is an object or item

explanation.surface: A phrase asking for the exact object.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'The', which grammar calls by this name; the rest of the clue builds it piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the word preceding a specific noun is known by this two-word term.

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of codes are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Wrong codes contrasted with correct beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' turns CODES into CREDO, and R for 'right' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeds or statements of faith, the principles a person holds.

parts.note: fabulous in its literal sense of belonging to fable: a mythical figure half man and half horse

explanation.definitionFit: A creature of Greek myth with a man's upper body on a horse's legs, so literally a fabled horse-man.

clue.text: O'Connor is unable to sing it

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a popular British singer and TV host
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: A joke that the entertainer O'Connor cannot carry a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Des O'Connor was a long-running British TV entertainer and singer, often teased for his singing. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter-melody sung above the main tune, so something a choir would perform.

indicators.note: framed says one word is set around another like a picture frame

parts.note: slight means slender or slim
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A thin sailor in a romantic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Glow from distant suns at night is a classic backdrop for lovers.

clue.text: Stay to keep graduate in check

indicators.note: in places the graduate inside the word for check

parts.note: a rein is a restraint or check
an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay put so as to keep a graduate under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' is only link wording here; the container is signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to linger or continue in one place.

indicators.note: heartens reads as 'in the hearts of', so the answer sits inside the words infant Asians

explanation.surface: Music that cheers up young children from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartens' looks like 'encourages' but tells you to look in the heart of 'infant Asians'.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-form instrumental composition, as in Disney's film of classical pieces.

indicators.note: converted says the letters of the two names are changed into another form

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruth Lane changes her faith away from Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' does double duty in the surface: it is the anagram signal, while 'from Catholicism?' hints at a Protestant who left Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Protestant church founded by the reformer who broke from Rome.

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: An assault that made a fool feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to assault or set upon someone.

clue.text: About to yield and present item again

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to submit is to give in

explanation.surface: An instruction concerning surrendering and re-presenting a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand in something once more for consideration.

clue.text: News items delivered bang on time

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the time word after the bang word

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, as of a gun
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Stories are handed in exactly when due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bang on time' reads as 'punctually', but splits into a gunshot sound placed before a long period. 'delivered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic accounts of events, the reporting of news.

clue.text: Paper label used by the rabble

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A newspaper tag employed by a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag describes a disorderly mob, as in ragtag and bobtail.

clue.text: Perishing whilst travelling to the US

definitions.meaning: slang for dying or being lost
heading west across the Atlantic from Britain

explanation.surface: Dying while on a trip to America.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang phrase for dying, and literally heading towards America from Europe.

clue.text: Horses racing quietly by the trees

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly
acers are maples

explanation.surface: Horses running softly past the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. Acer is the botanical name for maples.
explanation.definitionFit: Harness-racing horses that move both legs on one side together.

definitions.meaning: a char is a cleaning lady, or to char is to clean houses for pay

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady needs to earn some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidying is the cleaner's job; the slang sense is to win a large profit.

definitions.meaning: ... as in helpful work done for someone

explanation.surface: Gaining from a religious rite.
explanation.definitionFit: A good turn done for someone, and an act of public worship.

clue.text: Alarm a very loud mouthed Tory

parts.note: ff (fortissimo) is the musical mark for very loud
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: A frightening, very loud-mouthed Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthed' is surface padding attached to 'loud'; FF is fortissimo in musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning to frighten or terrify.

clue.text: Thrill when father's embracing one child

indicators.note: embracing says the father and child words hold the one word between them

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Excitement as a dad hugs one of his kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiver of excitement or a sudden tingle.

definitions.meaning: old naval slang for a midshipman; the 's is 'is'
a ... jacket is a short double-breasted coat

explanation.definitionFit: A junior naval officer, so called from reefing sails, and the short thick coat sailors wore.

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word team

parts.note: a wigging is a telling-off

explanation.surface: Grasping that the team captain needs a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link. A wigging is British slang for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Twigging is British slang for catching on or understanding.

definitions.meaning: wheat is a cereal crop, its seeds collectively
the smallest unit in imperial weight, about 65 milligrams

explanation.surface: Wheat is extremely light.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal seed in bulk, and a tiny unit of weight once based on one seed.

clue.text: Came in as ordered, but he's forgotten

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of came in as are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone arrived as instructed yet has lost his memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'commanded' but signals an anagram. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with memory loss, who cannot recall the past.

clue.text: Woman is upset t-just a shade

indicators.note: upset in a down-style turnaround says the words are read backwards here

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is distressed only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns both words round together. 't-just' is the OCR's rendering of a dash before 'just'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy brown or reddish pigment, a colour.

parts.note: ex means former
to pose is to model

explanation.surface: Disclosure by an ex-model.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure of scandal, a published unmasking.

indicators.note: about puts the jumbled letters around the one word
discord suggests the letters of intense clash into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fierce disagreement concerning a single scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discord' scrambles INTENSE into EINSTEN and 'about' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist famous for relativity, an archetypal scientist.
